b1-imperative.title: Imperative: Giving Commands
b1-imperative.pattern: tu/nous/vous forms of the present tense, minus the subject pronoun
b1-imperative.explanation: The imperative just drops the subject pronoun from the tu/nous/vous present-tense forms: "Parle !" (Speak!, tu), "Parlons !" (Let's speak!, nous), "Parlez !" (Speak!, vous). One quirk: -er verbs (and "aller") drop the final -s from the tu form: "tu parles" → "Parle !" not "Parles !". Negative commands wrap "ne...pas" around the verb as usual: "Ne parle pas !" (Don't speak!).
b1-imperative.fact: "Être", "avoir", and "savoir" have irregular imperatives borrowed from their subjunctive stems: "sois/soyons/soyez" (be), "aie/ayons/ayez" (have), "sache/sachons/sachez" (know) — these don't follow the normal drop-the-pronoun rule at all.

b1-subjunctive-intro.title: Present Subjunctive: Wishes, Wants, and Necessity
b1-subjunctive-intro.explanation: When one person wants or needs another to do something, French switches the second verb into the subjunctive after "que": "Je veux que tu viennes" (I want you to come), "Il faut que nous partions" (We need to leave). Most subjunctive stems come from the "ils" present-tense form minus -ent, plus these endings: -e/-es/-e/-ions/-iez/-ent. "Nous"/"vous" forms often match the imperfect instead.
b1-subjunctive-intro.fact: "Il faut que" (it is necessary that) is one of the most common subjunctive triggers in everyday French, used constantly for obligations: "Il faut que je parte" (I have to leave) — far more common in speech than the more formal "il est nécessaire que".

b1-relative-clauses.title: Relative Clauses: Connecting Ideas with Qui, Que, Où, Dont
b1-relative-clauses.pattern: qui (subject) · que (object) · où (place/time) · dont (of/about which, replaces de + noun)
b1-relative-clauses.explanation: "Qui" replaces the SUBJECT of the relative clause: "la femme qui parle" (the woman who is speaking). "Que" replaces the OBJECT: "le livre que je lis" (the book that I'm reading). "Où" replaces a place or time: "la ville où je suis né" (the city where I was born). "Dont" replaces anything introduced by "de": "le livre dont je parle" (the book I'm talking about, from "parler de").
b1-relative-clauses.fact: Unlike English, French never drops the relative pronoun — English allows "the book I read" with no "that," but French always requires "le livre que j'ai lu", "que" can never be omitted.

b1-time-expressions.title: Depuis, Pendant, Il y a: Talking About Duration
b1-time-expressions.pattern: depuis + present tense (ongoing) · pendant + duration (completed span) · il y a + time (ago)
b1-time-expressions.explanation: "Depuis" (since/for) pairs with the PRESENT tense for something still ongoing: "J'habite ici depuis trois ans" (I've lived here for three years — and still do). "Pendant" (for/during) describes a completed span, often with the passé composé: "J'ai vécu à Lyon pendant trois ans" (I lived in Lyon for three years — no longer). "Il y a" (ago) marks a point in the past: "Je suis arrivé il y a trois ans" (I arrived three years ago).
b1-time-expressions.fact: This depuis-with-present pattern is a classic difference from English, where "I have lived here for three years" uses a perfect tense — French uses the simple present because, from the speaker's perspective, the action is still happening right now.

b1-plus-que-parfait.title: Plus-que-parfait: An Action Before Another Past Action
b1-plus-que-parfait.explanation: The plus-que-parfait describes something that had already happened before another point in the past: "Quand je suis arrivé, ils avaient déjà commencé" (when I arrived, they had already started). It's built with the IMPERFECT of "avoir" or "être" plus the past participle — the same auxiliary-choice and agreement rules as the passé composé, just with the auxiliary itself pushed one step further into the past.
b1-plus-que-parfait.fact: This tense is what lets you clearly sequence two past events in a story — without it, "j'ai perdu mes clés que j'avais achetées" (I lost the keys I had bought) would collapse into ambiguous timing about which event came first.

items.en: The person who interviewed me was very nice.

items.fr: Depuis ce jour, je travaille dans cette entreprise avec plaisir.
items.en: Since that day, I've worked at that company happily.

lessons.title: A Reunion with Old Friends
lessons.titleNative: Des retrouvailles avec de vieux amis

items.fr: Nous ne nous étions pas vus depuis dix ans.
items.en: We hadn't seen each other in ten years.

items.fr: Le restaurant où nous nous sommes retrouvés était exactement le même qu'avant.
items.en: The restaurant where we met up was exactly the same as before.

items.fr: Il fallait que nous parlions pendant des heures pour tout se raconter.
items.en: We needed to talk for hours to catch up on everything.

items.fr: Depuis ce soir-là, nous nous voyons beaucoup plus souvent.
items.en: Since that evening, we see each other much more often.

items.fr: Avant de commencer ce nouveau travail, j'avais beaucoup hésité.
items.en: Before starting this new job, I had hesitated a lot.

items.fr: Il fallait que je sorte de ma zone de confort.
items.en: I needed to step out of my comfort zone.

items.fr: Les collègues que j'ai rencontrés sont devenus de vrais amis.
items.en: The colleagues I met became real friends.

items.fr: Depuis, je ne regrette absolument pas ce changement.
items.en: Since then, I absolutely don't regret this change.

lessons.title: A Lesson Learned the Hard Way
lessons.titleNative: Une leçon apprise à la dure

items.fr: Je n'avais jamais imaginé que cela pourrait mal se passer.
items.en: I had never imagined this could go wrong.

items.fr: Il fallait que j'accepte mon erreur pour pouvoir avancer.
items.en: I needed to accept my mistake in order to move forward.

items.fr: La leçon que j'ai apprise ce jour-là m'a beaucoup servi depuis.
items.en: The lesson I learned that day has served me well since.

items.fr: Depuis cette expérience, je réfléchis toujours deux fois avant d'agir.
items.en: Since that experience, I always think twice before acting.

items.fr: Nous n'avions pas parlé depuis des mois à cause d'un malentendu.
items.en: We hadn't spoken in months because of a misunderstanding.

items.fr: Il fallait que quelqu'un fasse le premier pas.
items.en: Someone needed to make the first move.

items.fr: La conversation que nous avons eue a tout changé entre nous.
items.en: The conversation we had changed everything between us.

items.fr: Depuis, notre relation est plus forte qu'avant.
items.en: Since then, our relationship is stronger than before.

items.fr: Il y a un an, je n'avais jamais touché un piano.
items.en: A year ago, I had never touched a piano.

items.fr: Il fallait que je pratique tous les jours pour progresser.
items.en: I needed to practice every day to progress.

items.fr: Le professeur qui m'a enseigné était incroyablement patient.
items.en: The teacher who taught me was incredibly patient.

items.fr: Depuis, jouer du piano est devenu ma plus grande passion.
items.en: Since then, playing piano has become my greatest passion.

items.fr: J'avais toujours eu peur de parler en public.
items.en: I had always been afraid of speaking in public.

items.fr: Il fallait que j'affronte cette peur un jour ou l'autre.
items.en: I needed to face that fear sooner or later.

items.fr: Le discours que j'ai donné ce jour-là a changé ma confiance en moi.
items.en: The speech I gave that day changed my self-confidence.

items.fr: Depuis, je n'ai plus jamais eu aussi peur de parler devant les autres.
items.en: Since then, I've never been as afraid to speak in front of others again.

items.fr: Il y a des années, j'avais promis à ma grand-mère de finir mes études.
items.en: Years ago, I had promised my grandmother I would finish my studies.

items.fr: Il fallait que je tienne cette promesse, quoi qu'il arrive.
items.en: I needed to keep that promise, whatever happened.

items.fr: Le jour où j'ai obtenu mon diplôme était l'un des plus beaux de ma vie.
items.en: The day I got my degree was one of the most beautiful of my life.

items.fr: Depuis, je sais que je peux accomplir tout ce que je me fixe comme but.
items.en: Since then, I know I can accomplish anything I set as a goal.

items.fr: Nous avons couvert beaucoup de choses, et tu as énormément progressé.
items.en: We've covered a lot, and you've progressed enormously.

items.fr: J'espère que tu continueras à pratiquer tout ce que tu as appris ici.
items.en: I hope you keep practicing everything you've learned here.

items.fr: La personne qui a commencé ce niveau n'est plus tout à fait la même aujourd'hui.
items.en: The person who started this level isn't quite the same today.

items.fr: Je suis certain que tu es prêt pour le niveau suivant.
items.en: I'm certain you're ready for the next level.
